quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Only the middle sound changes. Is it deep and rounded, or wide and bright?
quests.explanation: The word was "hot": the lips stay slightly rounded and the vowel comes from further back. "Hat" pulls the mouth wider and sounds brighter.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /æ/ is a front vowel with lips slightly spread; /ɒ/ is a back vowel with the lips rounded a little. The tongue moves from front to back and the lip shape changes with it.
quests.mouthPosition: For /æ/ keep the tongue pushed forward and the lips slightly spread. For /ɒ/ pull the tongue back and round the lips a little.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same first and last sounds here, so put all your attention on the vowel.
quests.explanation: "Map" has the bright, wide vowel, with the jaw dropped and the lips slightly spread. "Mop" sounds rounder and deeper in the mouth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Contrast the vowel colour: /æ/ sounds bright and sideways, /ɒ/ sounds deep and rounded.
quests.mouthPosition: Move your lips from a slight smile (/æ/) to a small round shape (/ɒ/) while the jaw stays open.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen for a spread, sideways vowel against a round, dark one.
quests.explanation: That was "tap", with the corners of the mouth pulled slightly apart. In "top" the lips round and the vowel drops deeper.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Front and unrounded for /æ/; back and lightly rounded for /ɒ/. Both are open, so listen for brightness rather than height.
quests.mouthPosition: Notice where the sound seems to resonate: at the front of the mouth for /æ/, deeper in the mouth for /ɒ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: One vowel is wide and bright, the other is short and dull. Which one is it?
quests.explanation: "Cat" is wide open and bright. "Cut" is a lazy, short vowel from the middle of the mouth, with hardly any jaw movement.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /æ/ is a front, open vowel made with the jaw low and lips slightly spread; /ʌ/ is a central, relaxed vowel that needs far less mouth opening.
quests.mouthPosition: For /æ/ drop the jaw and pull the corners of the mouth a little sideways. For /ʌ/ keep the mouth relaxed and only slightly open, with the tongue resting in the middle.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Is the mouth wide open in the middle of the word, or barely open?
quests.explanation: It was "bug", a short, dull vowel with a relaxed jaw. "Bag" would open the mouth wide and sound much brighter.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The tongue is forward and low for /æ/, but sits in the centre of the mouth for /ʌ/. To the ear, /æ/ sounds brighter and /ʌ/ sounds duller and flatter.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the front of your tongue rise toward your teeth for /æ/; for /ʌ/ the tongue stays lazy and flat.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The ends are identical. Listen for how open the mouth feels in the vowel.
quests.explanation: "Run" uses the lazy central vowel, so the mouth barely opens. In "ran" the jaw drops and the vowel widens.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Think 'wide and bright' for /æ/ against 'short and dull' for /ʌ/.
quests.mouthPosition: A big, wide mouth makes /æ/; a small, lazy mouth makes /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen for a tiny, tight vowel versus a big, open one.
quests.explanation: "Sit" keeps the teeth nearly together and the vowel short. "Sat" drops the jaw wide and sounds much fuller.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɪ/ is short and made with the jaw nearly closed; /æ/ is made with the jaw wide open. They are far apart in tongue height, so the biggest cue is how open the mouth is.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɪ/ the jaw barely moves. For /æ/ drop it well down and let the mouth widen.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: One vowel is thin and quick, the other is broad. Which do you hear?
quests.explanation: "Pan" has the wide-open vowel, and you can feel the jaw fall. "Pin" stays small and tight.
quests.vowelTensionRule: One vowel is small and tight (/ɪ/), the other is big and open (/æ/); the difference in openness is dramatic once you listen for it.
quests.mouthPosition: Go from nearly closed teeth (/ɪ/) to a wide, dropped jaw (/æ/) without changing anything else.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Notice how much the mouth would have to open to make the vowel.
quests.explanation: What you caught was "lip", with the jaw almost closed and a very short vowel. "Lap" would need a dropped jaw and a broader sound.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /æ/ sounds broad and full; /ɪ/ sounds thin and quick.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel your chin: it stays high for /ɪ/ and falls for /æ/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The vowel and ending are the same. Focus on the very first sound.
quests.explanation: "Ten" starts with a sharp burst as the tongue leaves the ridge behind the teeth. "Hen" starts with a soft breath and no closure at all.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /h/ is a breathy sound made in the throat with no tongue contact; /t/ is a stop made by pressing the tongue tip against the ridge behind the upper teeth, then releasing a burst.
quests.mouthPosition: For /h/ open the mouth and simply breathe out. For /t/ press the tongue tip against the ridge behind your upper teeth, then release.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the beginning: a hum with the lips closed, or a hiss?
quests.explanation: "Sad" begins with a thin hiss. "Mad" begins with a closed-lip hum, which sounds rounder and lower.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /m/ is a voiced hum made with closed lips and air through the nose; /s/ is a voiceless hiss made with the tongue tip near the ridge and air through the mouth.
quests.mouthPosition: For /m/ close the lips and hum. For /s/ open them, bring the tongue tip close to the ridge behind your teeth and blow a thin stream of air.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: At the start, is there a small burst from the lips, or a smooth glide?
quests.explanation: That was "red", where the sound glides in with no burst. "Bed" opens with a little pop from the lips.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /b/ is a lip stop with a small burst; /r/ is a smooth glide with no closure at all - the tongue tip curls back and the sound simply flows into the vowel.
quests.mouthPosition: For /b/ press the lips together and release. For /r/ keep the lips open, curl the tongue tip back and let the voice flow.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both begin with a breathy hiss. Listen to how sharp or soft it is.
quests.explanation: "Sun" starts with a sharp, high hiss made behind the teeth. "Fun" is softer and comes from the lip touching the teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /f/ is a soft hiss made between lower lip and upper teeth; /s/ is a sharper, higher hiss made with the tongue tip behind the teeth.
quests.mouthPosition: For /f/ bite the lower lip lightly and blow. For /s/ keep the lips apart and aim a narrow stream of air over the tongue tip.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen for a burst at the start versus just a breath.
quests.explanation: "Pop" begins with a clear lip burst that you can almost see. "Hop" begins with only a puff of breath.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /h/ is just breath from the throat; /p/ closes the lips completely and releases a burst of air.
quests.mouthPosition: For /p/ press both lips together, then pop them open. For /h/ keep the lips open and breathe out.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does the beginning hum through the nose, or does the tongue tip flick away?
quests.explanation: You heard "night", which starts with a nasal hum. In "light" the air flows around the tongue and the start is clearer and more open.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /l/ lets air flow around the sides of the tongue while the tip touches the ridge; /n/ blocks the mouth at the same place and sends the air through the nose.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch the tongue tip to the ridge behind the upper teeth. For /l/ let the sides of the tongue drop and air flow around; for /n/ seal the sides and hum through the nose.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: This time the difference is at the very end of the word. What closes the sound?
quests.explanation: "Cap" ends with the lips pressing shut. "Cat" ends with the tongue tip touching the ridge behind the teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the end of a word /p/ is closed with the lips and /t/ with the tongue tip. The vowel sounds different as it moves into each closure, and the final release differs in place.
quests.mouthPosition: For /p/ finish by pressing the lips together. For /t/ finish by pressing the tongue tip against the ridge behind the upper teeth.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the last sound: is it made in the throat area or at the front?
quests.explanation: It was "bat", with the closure at the tongue tip. "Back" finishes further back, with the tongue lifting to the soft palate.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Final /k/ is closed at the back of the tongue and /t/ at the tip. The closure position changes the very end of the vowel: deeper and duller into /k/, brighter into /t/.
quests.mouthPosition: For /k/ finish by lifting the back of the tongue to the soft palate. For /t/ finish with the tip against the ridge behind the teeth.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The vowel is the same; the ending is the whole difference.
quests.explanation: "Kick" ends with a hollow, back-of-the-tongue stop. "Kit" ends crisper and brighter at the tongue tip.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Final /k/ is closed at the back of the tongue and /t/ at the tip. The closure position changes the very end of the vowel: deeper and duller into /k/, brighter into /t/.
quests.mouthPosition: For /k/ finish by lifting the back of the tongue to the soft palate. For /t/ finish with the tip against the ridge behind the teeth.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Is the vowel long and smiling, or short and half-open?
quests.explanation: "Meet" stretches out with spread lips and a high tongue. "Met" is quick and the mouth opens a bit more.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /iː/ is long, tense and high; /e/ is short and mid. Both differ in duration and in how far the tongue rises.
quests.mouthPosition: For /iː/ spread the lips and lift the tongue high. For /e/ lower the jaw halfway and let the lips relax.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Compare how open the mouth is: nearly closed or wide?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "peach", with a long, smiling vowel and almost no jaw drop. "Patch" opens the jaw wide and cuts the vowel short.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /iː/ is long with a high tongue and spread lips; /æ/ is short with a low tongue and open jaw. They sit at opposite ends of the vowel space, so the mouth-opening difference is huge.
quests.mouthPosition: For /iː/ smile and lift the tongue high; for /æ/ drop the jaw and open wide.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the vowel before the final /l/ - long and tight, or short and open?
quests.explanation: "Hell" has the short, half-open vowel. "Heel" has a long, tense vowel that you hold before the /l/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /iː/ stretches and sounds tight; /e/ is crisp and sounds more open.
quests.mouthPosition: Smile for /iː/; drop the smile and open slightly for /e/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Is the vowel long and rounded, or short and relaxed?
quests.explanation: "Soon" pushes the lips forward into a tight round and holds the vowel. "Son" is short and lazy with no lip rounding.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /uː/ is long, high and rounded at the back; /ʌ/ is short, central and unrounded. Length and lip rounding both differ.
quests.mouthPosition: For /uː/ push the lips into a tight circle and raise the back of the tongue. For /ʌ/ keep the lips loose and open the jaw slightly.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both vowels are long and rounded. Listen for how open the jaw is.
quests.explanation: That was "call": a wider, lower, rounder vowel. "Cool" is tighter, with a nearly closed jaw and the lips pushed forward.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /uː/ is high, tightly rounded and often has slightly less back position than /ɔː/, which is lower and rounder. The difference is jaw opening.
quests.mouthPosition: For /uː/ close the jaw and make a small tight circle with the lips. For /ɔː/ open the jaw more and make a rounder, larger oval.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: One vowel holds still, the other slides. Which is which?
quests.explanation: "Pool" keeps the lips tightly rounded from start to finish. "Pole" begins relaxed and closes into a round only at the end.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /uː/ is a steady, high, rounded vowel; /əʊ/ starts in the centre and glides toward /ʊ/. One holds still, the other moves.
quests.mouthPosition: For /uː/ round the lips tightly from the beginning and hold. For /əʊ/ begin relaxed and gradually round.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does the vowel move as you say it, or does it stay still?
quests.explanation: The word was "pay", where the mouth begins half open and closes upward. "Pea" starts closed and stays there with a long smile.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /eɪ/ is a diphthong that glides upward and ends with a spread /ɪ/; /iː/ is a steady high vowel. Listen for movement versus stillness.
quests.mouthPosition: For /eɪ/ start with the jaw half open and close it toward the end. For /iː/ hold a wide smile with the jaw nearly closed.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen for a vowel that stays put or one that glides.
quests.explanation: "Bee" is one long, high, steady vowel. "Bay" opens a little and then glides up at the end.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The start differs: /eɪ/ begins with a half-open mouth, /iː/ begins and stays closed.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the jaw rise during /eɪ/; it stays high for /iː/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Focus only on the vowel: gliding or steady?
quests.explanation: "May" moves - the jaw rises during the vowel. "Me" is fixed in position with the lips spread wide.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /eɪ/ has two parts; /iː/ has one long, tight part.
quests.mouthPosition: Smile from the beginning of /iː/; for /eɪ/ the smile appears at the end.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Round and open, or tight and thin? Listen to the vowel.
quests.explanation: "Pot" has the open, rounded vowel from the back of the mouth. "Pit" is short, tight and bright.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɪ/ is a high front vowel with spread or neutral lips; /ɒ/ is an open back vowel with slightly rounded lips. They differ in almost every way: height, backness and lip shape.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɪ/ keep the jaw nearly shut and the tongue forward. For /ɒ/ drop the jaw and pull the tongue back with a little lip rounding.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Two short vowels: which one sounds crisp and which sounds dull?
quests.explanation: You heard "net", with a crisper, more forward vowel. "Nut" sounds flatter and duller.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /e/ is a front vowel with spread lips and the jaw half open; /ʌ/ is a central vowel that is lower and duller. Listen for bright versus dull.
quests.mouthPosition: For /e/ push the tongue forward and lift the front slightly. For /ʌ/ relax the tongue in the centre of the mouth.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Round and deep, or spread and forward? Listen in the middle of the word.
quests.explanation: "Log" has rounded lips and a deep vowel. "Leg" has a spread, forward vowel that sounds clearer and thinner.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /e/ is a front vowel with spread lips and a half-open jaw; /ɒ/ is a back vowel with rounded lips and a more open jaw. Front and unrounded against back and rounded.
quests.mouthPosition: For /e/ keep the tongue forward and the lips relaxed or slightly spread. For /ɒ/ pull the tongue back, drop the jaw and round the lips a little.
